trap_1_target_leakage.title: Trap 1: The 'Perfect — and Perfectly Useless' Columns (casual & registered)
trap_1_target_leakage.verdict: Using casual or registered as input features achieves artificial R² = 1.000 and MAE = 0.00. But ops cannot know rider category breakdowns before the hour happens! Our Dual-Head model solves this by modeling registered and casual independently using strictly antecedent calendar and weather data.

trap_2_shuffle_cheat.title: Trap 2: The 'Quietly Cheating' Random Train-Test Split
trap_2_shuffle_cheat.verdict: Random shuffling creates artificial interpolation between t-1 and t+1, leaking autocorrelation, future weather, and 2012 system growth trends into 2011. Honest chronological split reveals real out-of-sample error.

top_3_drivers.why_ops_needs_it: Ridership is dominated by weekday commuters. 08:00 AM spikes to ~477 rides/hr and 17:00-18:00 PM spikes to ~525 rides/hr, while overnight drops to <15 rides/hr.
top_3_drivers.ops_action: Schedule pre-balancing truck fleet runs between 05:30 - 07:30 AM to flood residential docks, and clear commercial docks by 16:00 PM.

top_3_drivers.driver_name: Thermal Comfort & Temperature Curve (temp_c, atemp_c, comfort_index)
top_3_drivers.why_ops_needs_it: Demand scales positively between 10°C and 27°C (+18.4 rides per +1°C rise). Below 8°C or above 36°C with high humidity, ridership drops drastically.
top_3_drivers.ops_action: Dynamically scale active fleet size and driver overtime based on next-day temperature forecasts. Reduce active depot shifts on freezing days (<5°C).

top_3_drivers.driver_name: Weather Severity & Rain Penalty (weathersit, severe_weather, hum_pct)
top_3_drivers.why_ops_needs_it: Precipitation creates an immediate modal shift to buses/taxis. Light rain causes a ~35% demand drop; heavy rain/snow slashes rides by 70-85%.
top_3_drivers.ops_action: Implement weather-triggered rebalancing stand-down: ground outdoor rebalancing vans to save fuel and maintenance during active rainstorms.
